records.name: Región de Murcia
records.summary: Assessed materially in line with the national position. Regional LGTBI or equality legislation is recorded for this region in the national policy inventories, but no region-specific incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified in the dedicated country dossier for this region; no sub-national facility, expression or assembly restriction exists anywhere in the country, and the 2023 national trans-equality law's implementation (including its education-facing parts) falls to the regional government. The national victimisation baseline applies here: a 2026 federation report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident.

records.name: Cataluña/Catalunya
records.summary: Assessed materially in line with the national position. No region-specific adverse incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified in the country dossier for this region (it sits outside the general inventory's flagged set). no region-specific incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified in the dedicated country dossier for this region; no sub-national facility, expression or assembly restriction exists anywhere in the country, and the 2023 national trans-equality law's implementation (including its education-facing parts) falls to the regional government. The national victimisation baseline applies here: a 2026 federation report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident. The region does contain one of the country's densest, most visible LGTBI urban centres with dedicated hate-crime structures within its own regional police force - the dossier's overall point being that in this country the fault line is city-versus-rural, not region-versus-region.

records.name: Cross River
records.summary: No state-specific trans-related source was found for this division in the current research pass: no local incident series and no documented enforcement divergence from the national frame. The national law applies here in full — the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 (up to 14 years, extends to tourists, bans LGBTQ+ organisations and public expression of identity) plus the inherited criminal provisions; national monitoring recorded 89 extortions, 118 harassment incidents and more than 20 unlawful detentions of LGBTQ+ people by law-enforcement officials in 2024 alone, with detentions for "looking gay" and release on payment of a bribe reported. This division sits outside the twelve northern states that carry a separate religious-law death-penalty regime for same-sex conduct. Dating-app "kito" extortion gangs are a nationwide app-user risk, and foreign government travel advice warns LGBT travellers of arrest, violence and blackmail.
